claims.claim_ar: الواو في «وَكَذَلِكَ» قد تعمل واو استئنافية أو حالية؛ أي أنها تربط الجملة بما قبلها أو تصف حالة، فتجعل الجملة مستأنفة/حالاً.
claims.claim_en: The waw in «وَكَذَلِكَ» can function as an istinaaf (resume/independent conjunction) or as a hal (circumstantial) waw, linking the sentence to what precedes or presenting it as a circumstance.
claims.needs_review_reason: The cited source explicitly gives two alternative analyses (استئنافية أو حالية); the commentary applies this diagnosis to other verses, so application to this ayah should be verified in context.

claims.claim_ar: قد تُقرأ الواو في مبتدأ الجملة («وَكَذَلِكَ ...») كواو عاطفة تربط الجملة بسياقها السابق وتؤدي وظيفة الربط التأكيدي.
claims.claim_en: The initial waw in the sentence can be read as a coordinating waw (waaw 'atf), linking the sentence to the prior context and serving a connective/emphatic function.
claims.needs_review_reason: Source comment labels the waw as 'عاطفة' in some contexts; there is variation among commentators whether it is purely connective or has other nuances—confirm with tafsir-specific sources for this ayah.

claims.claim_ar: الجملة التي تبدأ بـ «وَكَذَلِكَ...» تُعرض هنا بصيغة مستأنفة مسوقة؛ أي أنها مُقدمة لتفسير أو تمثيل يُقَدَّم لإيضاح أمر سابق.
claims.claim_en: The sentence beginning with «وَكَذَلِكَ...» is presented as a resumed, 'masooq' (introduced) clause — i.e., an introductory/resumptive sentence that supplies an exemplification or clarification of what preceded.
claims.needs_review_reason: The source remark about 'الجملة مستأنفة مسوقة' refers generally to the discourse function of such clauses in the Qur'anic style; applying it to this specific ayah is plausible but should be cross-checked with tafsir/بلاغة treatments focused on S6:75.

warnings: The available source chunks are general i'rab/بلاغة comments on various verses (not all are direct exegesis of S6:75). Quotations used are taken from those chunks and may refer to analogous constructions elsewhere; corroboration with direct tafsir/بلاغة on S6:75 is recommended.
